draft.title: Hormones and physical activity
card: Hormones are chemical messengers made in the body. Their levels change over time, and the menstrual cycle is one example of a regular change.
During the menstrual cycle, levels of hormones such as oestrogen and progesterone rise and fall. Some people notice changes in energy, mood, sleep or how hard exercise feels at different times.
These effects differ a great deal from person to person. Many people can train well in every phase of the cycle.
An athlete or coach can track the cycle and notice patterns. They can then consider adjusting training, such as its intensity or recovery time, to suit how the athlete feels.
draft.remember: Hormone levels change, and each athlete can use their own patterns to help plan training.

a.q: Why might an athlete track her menstrual cycle when planning training?
opts: To spot personal patterns and adjust training to suit
To learn which phase she must avoid training in
To prove that her performance is lower in some phases
To make her training the same as every other athlete's
a.why: Tracking shows an athlete's own patterns, so she and her coach can consider changes to intensity or recovery. The option about avoiding a phase is wrong because the card says many people can train well in every phase.
a.clue: Think about what tracking shows for one person.

b.q: Tess, a netballer in Geelong, notices that her energy is often low and training feels harder in the days before her period. Her coach wants a sensible response. What should they do?
opts: Consider lighter sessions or extra recovery in those days
Remove her from training in that part of every cycle
Assume every player on the team has the same pattern
Ignore the pattern, as hormones never affect training
b.why: Tess's pattern is her own, so the coach can consider adjusting intensity or recovery to suit how she feels. Removing her from training every cycle goes too far, because effects differ between people and many athletes can train well in every phase.
b.clue: Use Tess's own pattern, and do not assume it applies to everyone.

a.best: To spot personal patterns and adjust training to suit

b.best: Consider lighter sessions or extra recovery in those days
